label: start of copy phase (<DEL> step / first copy step) in sequences beginning with x or i
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.013% of steps). About 92% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) or the first copy step (recall_idx 1); it never fires at recall_idx >= 2 and almost never during the original phase (a small amount at orig_idx 8, just before <DEL> in L=9 sequences). Within those two steps it is almost only active when the first original token is x or i (89% of mass), and enriched when the token being recalled is x or i (out_tok x 33x lift, i 11x): e.g. <DEL> in x-initial sequences, or the copy step that inputs i and outputs x/i in i-initial sequences. Activity also depends on absolute time (peaks at t=5, i.e. L=4 first copy step, and at t=8-9, i.e. <DEL> for L=8-9). The predicate gets 81% recall and mass recall but only ~1% precision: the feature fires on only a small fraction of the x/i-initial copy-start steps, and none of the history variables I tried (orig(1) in {x,i}, L, next_out) picks out that fraction well (best F1 ~0.25 for recall_idx==1 & first_tok==i & out_tok in {x,i}). Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.118, max 0.206). The highest activations are at <DEL> in long x-x-initial sequences. Does not fire on other first tokens (a, b, f etc. give zero) or later in the copy.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=i (+5.42), orig0=x (+4.80), L=4 & t=5 (+4.24), orig1=x (+4.10), orig1=i (+3.38), orig0=n (+3.20). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.59), to_go=5 (-2.50), prev2_tok=h (-1.89), t=10 (-1.84).
